Eight places to go deeper than this lesson, or to check a citation yourself before it goes in a
real Lakeshore document. All were checked and loading at the time this page was written.

- **[FDA guidance page: Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP — Questions and Answers](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/data-integrity-and-compliance-drug-cgmp-questions-and-answers)**
  — FDA's own December 2018 guidance page for the source this whole module is built on. Read the
  full Q&A list once: this lesson only used the ALCOA, metadata, and "systems" questions, and the
  rest covers audit trails, static/dynamic records, and backups that later modules in this course
  pick up directly.

- **[21 CFR 211.68, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/211.68)**
  — the automatic/mechanical/electronic equipment section this curriculum has used since
  `csv-and-becs`, and one of the drug-CGMP sections FDA's own footnote ties to ALCOA's "accurate"
  element. Worth rereading alongside this lesson's citation decoder.

- **[21 CFR 210.2, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/210.2)**
  — the supplementation clause that lets a drug-CGMP guidance like this one reach a blood
  establishment's own records at all. Already the subject of its own full lesson in
  `gamp5-and-the-v-model`; this page is here so you can check the exact text yourself without
  re-deriving it.

- **[Overview of Data Integrity (4of11) GCP Data Integrity Workshop](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BTFn9dYoz34)**
  (U.S. Food and Drug Administration, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this
  lesson, from FDA's own channel. It comes from a clinical-research (GCP) workshop, not blood
  establishments or drug CGMP, so use it for the general idea of data integrity rather than for any
  citation here. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[PIC/S PI 041-1: Good Practices for Data Management and Integrity in Regulated GMP/GDP Environments](https://picscheme.org/docview/4234)**
  — the international inspectorates' guidance (a 63-page PDF dated 1 July 2021 on its cover). This
  is the kind of international-regulator source the "ALCOA+" vocabulary comes from. Read its
  data-integrity definition and attribute list to see the industry-and-international practice this
  lesson keeps separate from FDA's five-letter ALCOA, and don't mistake it for FDA guidance.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[MHRA (UK): GxP data integrity guidance](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-on-gxp-data-integrity)**
  — the UK regulator's own publication page for its GxP data-integrity guidance. This is the
  MHRA this lesson refers to generally; it is a UK document, so read it for how another regulator
  frames the same problem, not as something that binds Lakeshore. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[WHO Technical Report Series No. 1033, Annex 4: Guideline on data integrity](https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/medicines/norms-and-standards/guidelines/inspections/trs1033-annex4-guideline-on-data-integrity.pdf)**
  — the World Health Organization's data-integrity guideline (a PDF whose first page says it
  replaces the earlier WHO Annex 5 on good data and record management practices). A third
  international voice to compare with FDA's and PIC/S's, and useful if a vendor or auditor cites
  "WHO expectations." Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP Questions and Answers (guidance PDF)](https://www.fda.gov/media/119267/download)**
  — the guidance itself as a PDF, rather than the landing page listed above. Read it with the
  question numbers visible when you want to check the exact wording of the ALCOA, metadata, and
  systems answers quoted in this lesson against FDA's own copy. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about ALCOA+ and data integrity.

- **[ALCOA+ and Data Integrity](https://www.pharmtech.com/view/alcoa-and-data-integrity)** (Pharmaceutical Technology) — A trade-press explainer that walks through each ALCOA+ attribute with practical examples; a readable second take on the five letters before you apply them to a real record. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200). Page title checked.
- **[The Challenges of Ensuring Laboratory Data Integrity](https://www.gmp-compliance.org/gmp-news/the-challenges-of-ensuring-laboratory-data-integrity)** (ECA Academy) — A practitioner article showing where data-integrity problems actually arise in instrument-driven workflows, which is the kind of system the lesson's example record lives in. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200). Page title checked.
- **[GAMP Guide: Records & Data Integrity](https://ispe.org/publications/guidance-documents/gamp-records-pharmaceutical-data-integrity)** (ISPE) — The catalog page for ISPE's records and data integrity guide. The guide itself is a paid publication; the page is worth reading for its table of contents, which shows how practitioners organize the topic. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200). Page title checked.
